relations.subject: Francis Woodman Cleaves
relations.evidence: Cleaves received his undergraduate degree in Classics from Dartmouth College

relations.subject: Francis Woodman Cleaves
relations.evidence: enrolled in the graduate program in Comparative Philology at Harvard... In the following year he received his Ph.D.

relations.subject: Francis Woodman Cleaves
relations.evidence: transferred to the study of Far Eastern Languages under Serge Elisséeff in the mid-1930s

relations.subject: Francis Woodman Cleaves
relations.evidence: In 1935, on a fellowship from the Harvard-Yenching Institute, Cleaves went first to Paris, where he studied Mongolian and other Central Asian languages with the Sinologist Paul Pelliot for three years

relations.subject: Francis Woodman Cleaves
relations.evidence: then to Beijing where he studied with the Mongolist Antoine Mostaert S.J.

relations.subject: Francis Woodman Cleaves
relations.evidence: taught at Harvard University... Cleaves returned to Harvard in 1941 and taught Chinese... proceeded to teach Chinese and Mongolian, without interruption, for the next thirty-five years... Cleaves reluctantly retired in 1980

relations.subject: Joseph Fletcher

relations.subject: Elizabeth Endicott-West
relations.evidence: Among his best-known disciples were Joseph Fletcher, the distinguished Mongolist and historian, and Elizabeth Endicott-West

relations.subject: Francis Woodman Cleaves
relations.evidence: Cleaves had an especially close relation with William Hung, a preeminent scholar who had become his friend and mentor when they met in China in the 1930s.
